macro_news_facts: USDJPY rose to 158.17 during Tokyo afternoon as euro weakness triggered broad dollar buying.
By 17:00 JST USDJPY had fallen back to around 157.65-157.67 after Takaichi stressed fiscal sustainability and control of bond issuance.
At 19:34 JST USDJPY had rebounded to around 157.93-157.95, leaving the pair near the prior Friday close and without a clean directional break.
Oil eased as Middle East exports increased and G7 emergency-stock releases reduced immediate supply fears.
U.S. Treasury yields eased slightly from recent highs but remained elevated; 10-year yields were around the mid-5.2% area in London-session reporting.
Japan 30-year JGB yield hit a record 4.235%, showing fiscal-duration stress remains significant despite Takaichi's reassurance.

facts: USDJPY traded as high as 158.17 today but failed to sustain the breakout.
Takaichi's fiscal-discipline remarks were followed by yen buying and USDJPY around 157.65-157.67 at 17:00.
USDJPY then rebounded to roughly 157.93-157.95 by 19:34.
Japan 30-year JGB yield reached a record 4.235%, so fiscal-duration stress has not disappeared.
U.S. ISM Services PMI is scheduled for 23:00 JST tonight.
interpretations: The 12:57 SLIGHT_USDJPY_DOWN view was only partially supported: yen strength appeared after the 158.17 rejection and Takaichi speech, but it did not persist into London.
The intraday sequence now looks more like a two-way range than a clean yen-strengthening trend.
Dollar support from broad dollar strength and still-high U.S. yields is being offset by Japan fiscal-discipline messaging, BOJ tightening risk, intervention risk, and weaker U.S. labor data.
The next meaningful directional discriminator is tonight's ISM Services release; pre-release conviction should remain limited.
change_since_prior: MATERIAL_CHANGE: after the 12:57 observation USDJPY first rallied through 158.00 to 158.17, then reversed to about 157.65 after Takaichi's fiscal-discipline message, and rebounded to around 157.94 by 19:34. The earlier slight-down view has weakened into a range/neutral state.
base_case: NEUTRAL_RANGE: USDJPY remains broadly contained around the high-157s, with 158.17 as today's failed upside extension and roughly 157.4-157.6 as the intraday support zone before the 23:00 ISM catalyst.
alternative_case: USDJPY_UP_BREAK: a strong ISM services result and/or renewed U.S. yield rise pushes the pair sustainably above today's 158.17 high toward the broader 158.4-158.6 resistance area.
